tagline: Named, said the judge, because it runs toward the woods.
intro: Woodward starts beside Hart Plaza, a few hundred feet from the Detroit River, and runs north-northwest through downtown, Midtown and New Center. At 8 Mile it leaves the city for the Oakland County suburbs, Ferndale and Royal Oak and Birmingham, and goes on as a broad boulevard to Pontiac. The blocks along it were once nicknamed Piety Hill, and 22 of its churches in Detroit and Highland Park are on the National Register.

It follows the Saginaw Trail, an Indian path, and was laid in logs in 1817 and oak planks in 1848. Judge Augustus Woodward, taken to task for naming it after himself, answered that it was called Woodward because it ran wood-ward, toward the woods.

moments.title: Ford Piquette Avenue Plant
moments.text: A brick factory of 355 windows, built like a New England mill in 1904, where Ford first built the Model T and tried out a moving assembly line.

moments.title: 6 Mile to 7 Mile
moments.text: In 1909 this stretch became the first mile of concrete road in the country, at a cost of $14,000.

moments.title: Woodward Dream Cruise
moments.text: On the third Saturday of August some 40,000 vehicles, mostly from the 1950s through the early 70s, cruise the avenue from Ferndale to Pontiac.
